title: LAF Drawing Competition 2026: Submit Your Artwork (15–30 June)
excerpt: Children ages 1–18 can upload paintings and drawings to the Lata Agrawal Foundation competition. Browse the gallery, vote by age group, and celebrate creativity in Wardha and across India.
html:
The Lata Agrawal Foundation (LAF) Drawing Competition is open from 15 June to 30 June 2026. Children across India can share original artwork on the theme Education, hope, and community.

Parents verify their email with a one-time code to upload safely. Appropriate entries appear in the public gallery right away. Supporters can sign in with Google to vote — one vote per account per drawing, with winners announced by age group.

Who can participate?

Any child aged 1–18 may enter with a parent or guardian. We show only the child's first name, age group, class, school, and city publicly — never full contact details.

How to submit

Visit our Submit artwork page, verify your email, and upload a JPEG, PNG, or WebP image (max 5 MB). You can also browse the gallery and vote for favourites.

Why we run this event

Art builds confidence and joy in learning. LAF works with communities in Wardha, Maharashtra and beyond to support children's education, nutrition, and wellbeing. This competition connects young artists with supporters who care about the same values.

title: How LAF Supports Education for Village Children in Wardha
excerpt: Learn how the Lata Agrawal Foundation helps underprivileged children in Wardha, Maharashtra access learning support, nutrition, and community programmes — and how you can help.
html:
The Lata Agrawal Foundation is a registered NGO based in Wardha, Maharashtra. We work with local communities so children can attend school regularly, eat nutritious meals, and access learning resources — regardless of family income.

Education at the centre

We partner with schools and community centres to provide tutoring, learning materials, and digital literacy. Our free Learning Resource Library offers curated links for students, volunteers, and NGOs across India.

Health and nutrition camps

Regular health camps — including dental and eye check-ups at Sewashram Wardha — help children stay healthy enough to learn. These events are made possible by donors and volunteers.

Get involved

You can donate, volunteer your time, or explore other ways to help. Every contribution supports real programmes on the ground in Wardha and partner communities.

title: Volunteer with LAF: Mentor, Teach, and Support Children in India
excerpt: Volunteering with the Lata Agrawal Foundation is a practical way to support children's education in Wardha and online. Discover roles, time commitments, and how to apply.
html:
Volunteers are the backbone of the Lata Agrawal Foundation (LAF). Whether you live in Wardha or contribute remotely from anywhere in India or abroad, your skills can help children learn and grow.

What volunteers do

Common roles include tutoring, organising food drives, helping at health camps, reviewing learning resources for our library, and supporting events like the Drawing Competition.

Time and commitment

Some volunteers give a few hours monthly; others support specific campaigns. We match skills with needs — teaching, logistics, communications, or technology.

Apply today

Read more on our volunteer page or contact us to discuss how you can help. CSR partners can also explore structured programmes on our CSR page.

title: Free Learning Resource Library for Students and NGOs in India
excerpt: LAF's Learning Resource Library curates free educational links for students, trainers, and NGOs. Browse robotics, scholarships, volunteer training, and more.
html:
The Lata Agrawal Foundation maintains a free, curated Learning Resource Library for students, teachers, volunteers, and NGO partners across India.

What's inside

Resources are organised by topic — including robotics, scholarships, NGO tools, and volunteer training — with learning paths that guide beginners step by step.

Who it's for

Students preparing for exams, trainers running community classes, and NGOs looking for vetted links can all use the library at no cost. Community members can also suggest new resources.

Explore and share

Visit the library homepage, browse learning paths, and share useful pages with schools in Wardha and beyond. Support our mission with a donation if you are able.
